message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe.

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average; ^1H ≈ 1.00794 u, ^2H ≈ 2.01410 u) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Group/Period** | Group 1A (alkali metals), Period 1 |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) at 1 atm |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) at 1 atm |
| **Density (at STP)** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 kg m⁻³) |
| **Molar volume (ideal gas)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ (at 273.15 K, 1 atm) |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Isotopes** | ^1H (protium, 99.98 %), ^2H (deuterium, 0.02 %) – stable; ^3H (tritium) – radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 y). |
| **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds; diatomic H₂ is the most common form. Can also form hydrides with metals or nonmetals. |
| **Acidity/basicity** | Acts as a very weak acid (pKa ≈ 35) when protonated to H₃⁺; forms hydride ions (H⁻) in metal hydrides. |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; burns in air to produce water (combustion reaction). Combines with oxygen, chlorine, fluorine, etc. |
| **Uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), industrial feedstock (ammonia synthesis, methanol production), cryogenic coolant, laboratory standard gas, space propulsion. |
| **Physical appearance** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless, non‑metallic gas. |
| **Safety notes** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (range 4–75 % vol.). Requires careful handling and proper ventilation. |

---

### Quick Facts

* **Lightest element** – lowest atomic mass among all elements.  
* **Most abundant element** – makes up about 75 % of the elemental mass of the observable universe.  
* **Only element with one valence electron** – gives it unique reactivity patterns.  
* **Key role in astrophysics** – fuels stellar fusion processes (pp chain, CNO cycle).  

Feel free to ask if you’d like more detail on any specific property!
